Audits 2504/2521: exact Artifact Registry upload and native repository consumption

This procedure leaves all external cases not_run until executed by the repository
owner. Preparation hashes local files only. The consumer downloads packages using
native APT/DNF, checks exact bytes and package metadata, and retains evidence. It
does not install a package or mutate system repositories, IAM, VMs or services.
No new CI job is needed. Existing native 2352 install/upgrade/removal results must
already cover precisely these candidate bytes; this procedure binds repository
retrieval to those results. It does not claim an online service-upgrade journey.

Original scope
PR2521 (cf3e5d6df) already forced `_rpmformat 4` and checked the produced six-byte
RPM lead edabeedb0300. PR2504 (5626af09e) pinned Ubuntu 24 packaging after GCP rejected
newer-produced RPMs. Neither establishes acceptance just because rpm can read the
file. The current shared build-linux-packages.sh and real native guest tests cover
format and package transactions. External upload/index/download remains distinct.

1. Select a real release candidate and evidence
Use the exact full source commit, completed build.yml run URL and native package
job artifacts linux-packages-{deb,rpm}-{amd64,arm64}. Each contains wendy and
wendy-agent. Download via the approved GitHub artifact/release mechanism, retain
artifact IDs/digests and release attestation verification, and hash all eight
package files. Do not repackage or rename the version to make an upload pass.
Use the existing native package guest evidence for these exact hashes, including
normal result.json with the embedded manifest, and retain its original stopped
upgrade negative-control results too. A result for another source or package hash
cannot qualify this release. In a release run these are the package-linux outputs
before attestation. Existing successful PR test binaries are not release artifacts.

On a native metadata host, record exact package names/versions/architectures:
  dpkg-deb -f PACKAGE.deb Package Version Architecture
  rpm -qp --qf '%{NAME}\n%{VERSION}-%{RELEASE}\n%{ARCH}\n' PACKAGE.rpm
Do not infer RPM version from the Git tag: packaging replaces version hyphens
with underscores and includes its release field. The generator requires all
eight release items and checks their hashes against native normal-transaction
proofs. It refuses RPMs without the expected 3.0 lead before producing uploads.

2. Reserve the external context before any upload
The owner chooses one of two contexts and records who approved the exact project,
repository resource names, version/hashes, credentials role and cleanup authority.
Credentials must stay out of inventory, command logs, archives and Git.

For an already authorized stable release, use mode=authorized-release, location
us-central1 and repositories wendy-apt/wendy-yum. Use only the ordinary existing
publish-linux-repos job in that exact build.yml release run. It performs the real
APT and YUM uploads after native packaging. Do not dispatch a new production
release, repeat uploads, change version, or create an external service just to
collect evidence. The generated plan emits no manual uploads in this mode.
Save that job's exact artifact selection, successful gcloud operations and log URL.

For a separately owner-reserved trial, use mode=reserved and fresh repository
names wendy-audit-TRIAL_FIRST16-apt and wendy-audit-TRIAL_FIRST16-yum in an approved
project/location. The owner can create these standard private repositories using:
  gcloud artifacts repositories create REPO --project=PROJECT --location=LOCATION --repository-format=apt
  gcloud artifacts repositories create REPO --project=PROJECT --location=LOCATION --repository-format=yum
Apply repository-scoped roles/artifactregistry.writer to the approved uploader
and roles/artifactregistry.reader to the consumer VM service account through the
owner's IAM process. Do not grant project-wide writer access, create long-lived
service-account keys, enable public access, or reuse unrelated repositories.
Keep the actual creation/describe/IAM review records. An existing repository with
the same name must be investigated, not silently adopted or deleted.

In either context inspect `gcloud artifacts repositories describe REPO` with the
explicit project/location. Require the exact full resource, APT/YUM format and
STANDARD_REPOSITORY mode, expected owner, and no remote/virtual upstream that can
mask a failed upload. Keep both describe JSON responses. The generated describe
and settings commands use explicit resources and have a 600s local guardian bound.
No credentials are read or used during plan generation.

3. Qualify four disposable native consumer VMs
Use owner-reserved Compute Engine VMs, one each for deb-amd64, deb-arm64,
rpm-amd64 and rpm-arm64. Record project, zone, immutable instance ID, exact image
resource/version and responsible owner. The two DEB VMs use a supported Ubuntu
or Debian image and the real Artifact Registry APT transport. The two RPM VMs
use a supported Enterprise Linux image with DNF4, dnf-plugins-core's download
command and the matching dnf-plugin-artifact-registry package. DNF5 and emulation
are outside this qualified consumer script. Provisioning is an explicit owner
operation, never an automatic side effect of the tests. Select actual available
image versions/native machine types; do not invent an arm64 image identifier.

Use a dedicated VM service account with reader access only to the selected
repositories and the required cloud-platform access scope. Configure the native
Artifact Registry clients using Google's current supported distro instructions:
  https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/os-packages/debian/configure
  https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/os-packages/rpm/configure
For GCE, the helpers use the VM service account. Do not export an OAuth token or
copy personal gcloud/ADC credentials to the guest. Complete client/plugin setup
before capturing the boot/OS/tool identities; an unsupported helper/distro is a
qualification failure, not a reason to turn off authentication or use curl alone.
The owner reviews the exact output of the generated `gcloud beta artifacts
print-settings apt|yum` commands; do not execute remote text blindly.

The consumer creates its own repository files, caches and lists under a fresh
output path. Its APT signed-by key is the reviewed Artifact Registry regional
repository keyring; acquire it from the official LOCATION-apt.pkg.dev signing-key
endpoint, convert with gpg --dearmor in a private output, and retain its observed
fingerprint/hash and provenance. No system keyring is changed by the consumer.
YUM metadata GPG validation is unsupported by Artifact Registry; its documented
HTTPS configuration uses repo_gpgcheck=0. This procedure additionally checks all
downloaded bytes against exact approved release SHA256 and native package proof.
It does not call that a package-signature verification.

As the reserved unprivileged guest user, record:
  cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
  sha256sum /etc/os-release
  uname -m
  systemd-detect-virt --vm
  systemd-detect-virt --container
  sha256sum /usr/bin/apt-get /usr/bin/dpkg-deb       # DEB guest
  sha256sum /usr/bin/dnf /usr/bin/rpm               # RPM guest
  dnf --version                                  # RPM guest must be 4.x
The container check must report none with exit 1; the VM check must succeed.
Observe instance/id, instance/zone and project/project-id through the authenticated
GCE metadata protocol with Metadata-Flavor:Google, and independently match them
to the owner's VM reservation. The consumer rechecks these against its plan and
ignores proxy variables for metadata. Never run it on the developer host.
Reserve sufficient private disk for two package files plus metadata, at least 2 GiB.

4. Prepare the local inventory and plan
Inventory fields:
  trial: fresh 32 lowercase hex
  source_commit: exact 40 lowercase hex
  release_run: https://github.com/wendylabsinc/WendyOS/actions/runs/ACTUAL_ID
  target: {mode: reserved|authorized-release, project: ACTUAL_PROJECT,
           location: ACTUAL_LOCATION, apt: EXACT_APT_REPO, yum: EXACT_YUM_REPO}
  records: {authorization: FILE, release_provenance: FILE,
            repository_identity: FILE, guest_reservation: FILE, cleanup: FILE}
  apt_keyring: REVIEWED_LOCAL_GPG_FILE
  apt_keyring_sha256: its actual 64 hex digest
  packages: eight objects, each {format: deb|rpm, architecture: amd64|arm64,
            name: wendy|wendy-agent, version: EXACT_NATIVE_VERSION, path: PACKAGE,
            sha256: ACTUAL_DIGEST, native_result: MATCHING_NORMAL_RESULT_JSON}
  guests: four keys deb-amd64, deb-arm64, rpm-amd64, rpm-arm64, each containing
          {instance_id: OBSERVED_DECIMAL_ID, project: ACTUAL_PROJECT, zone: ZONE,
           boot_id: OBSERVED_UUID, os_release_sha256: DIGEST,
           client_sha256: APT_OR_DNF_DIGEST, metadata_tool_sha256: DPKG_OR_RPM_DIGEST}

Use actual JSON string/array/object syntax. All FILE entries are nonempty local
evidence paths. Run from the candidate checkout:
  python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/artifact-registry-rehearsal.py prepare INVENTORY NEW_PLAN
Inspect plan.json, commands.json and prepared-files.json. There are no image or
package payload copies in the plan; references remain hash-bound to local release
files. The output contains the consumer, guardian, reviewed keyring and this guide.
The generator does not call gcloud, package clients, network services or guests.

5. Execute the authorized upload and collect receipts
Rehash original candidate files before and after the upload. In reserved mode,
execute each generated upload-N argv exactly once from the approved uploader
environment. Capture stdout, stderr, command, start/end time, exit status and
operation/service response, indexed by the exact source file hash. A timeout or
ambiguous response is unknown; inspect the service before deciding any retry.
In authorized-release mode retain the existing publish job's actual corresponding
evidence instead. Repository existence, RPM lead, a valid local file, or a green
unrelated release cannot substitute for successful candidate uploads.
Check the exact expected package versions become indexed in each target; retain
the native consumer's metadata output. Do not upload a deliberately incompatible
RPM to a production repository as a negative control.

6. Consume through actual native repository clients
Copy the prepared directory to each reserved guest without changing file bytes.
Independently compare prepared-files.json to the uploader's retained copy, and
verify every file hash before execution. No candidate package files should be
present in the new consumer output or cache. Execute as the admitted non-root user:
  python3 PLAN/guardian.py --timeout 900 -- python3 PLAN/acceptance.py consume PLAN/plan.json GUEST_KEY --confirm-trial TRIAL --output NEW_GUEST_OUTPUT
The outer guardian owns the complete command group; each native client operation also has a 300s bound and 30s network timeout.
The fresh APT lists/sourceparts or DNF reposdir/cache expose only the selected
repository. Exact version and native architecture selectors prevent accidentally
testing the latest release or another repository's package. Download success must
be followed by an exact hash set and native metadata match for both packages.
Unknown or duplicate/extra files, hash/version/architecture mismatch, changed guest
identity or client bytes fail. A cached package is not accepted as new evidence.

Keep result.json, metadata.log, download.log, source/client configs, actual package
files/hashes and the guest's final identity. Each result must say passed and retain
the same plan SHA. It deliberately leaves external_acceptance pending_upload_review:
only an independent owner can join the actual upload receipt, candidate provenance,
repository identity and all four consumer outputs. Per-architecture omissions stay
pending. The exact-byte native 2352 results establish install/upgrade behavior of
those bytes; fetching packages alone does not establish a newly executed install.

7. Preserve evidence and retire only owned resources
Hash and archive the private plan, actual receipts and all four guest results.
Review logs for credentials before sharing; no model/media/package assets enter
Git. Test failures retain output directories for diagnosis. The consumer never
cleans an unknown directory or alters a system package database.
The owner retires the four exact reserved VMs via the approved VM cleanup record.
Only in reserved mode, after exported evidence is verified, describe each exact
nonce-named repository again and delete that resource through the owner's change
process. Keep deletion receipts. Never delete production wendy-apt/wendy-yum,
unrelated packages, IAM bindings or caches. Uncertain operation state stays unknown.

Source references (commands checked 2026-11-13)
https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/artifacts/apt/upload
https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/artifacts/yum/upload
https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/artifacts/repositories/create
https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/beta/artifacts/print-settings/apt
https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/beta/artifacts/print-settings/yum
https://dnf-plugins-core.readthedocs.io/en/latest/download.html

Existing release-job acceptance alternative
------------------------------------------
The existing publish-linux-repos job now runs
.github/scripts/publish-linux-repositories.py in its unchanged stable-release
publication context. It preserves each native candidate's identity, byte hash,
upload exit status and upload-log hash. After all eight uploads succeed, fresh
APT and DNF4 configurations fetch the exact CLI/Agent versions for amd64 and
arm64 and require the downloaded bytes to match those receipts. A wrong-hash
control must fail. The job uses the existing action's short-lived WIF credentials
with Google's real transport helpers; it does not provision a new identity.

The native x86_64 clients run in owned pinned containers and select both package
architectures. This is repository metadata/download evidence, not ARM execution
or a second installation/upgrade test. The existing native installed-package
gates retain responsibility for actual installation and service lifecycle.
No Wendy package is installed in the release acceptance containers or host.

The required result is repository-consumer-evidence/result.json with status
passed, eight successful upload receipts, four successful consumer results and
proven removal of both owned containers. The evidence includes candidate/source,
helper and key hashes and native client/dependency versions. Credentials, caches
and downloaded package copies are not uploaded as evidence. The job's existing
if/needs conditions still govern publication; preparing this check does not run
or authorize a release. Until an actual authorized release produces these
receipts, external Artifact Registry acceptance remains pending.
